fields.h1: Build a Silent Auction Form That Logs Items, Bids and Winners
fields.hero_description: Describe your items and bidding rules. Emergent builds the silent auction form, the bids table behind it and a winners list for closing time.
fields.features_heading: What Paper Bid Sheets Leave to Volunteers
fields.features_subheading: A clipboard collects names and amounts. These six pieces handle what volunteers would otherwise check by hand.
fields.feature_1:
Bids checked against the high bid

Set an opening bid and a minimum increment for each item. Any bid under the current high plus that increment comes back to the guest with the exact amount they need to beat.
fields.feature_2:
A QR code on every bid card

Print a QR code for each item on its table card. Guests scan it with a phone and type a bidder number and an amount. The bid lands in the one table that every item shares.
fields.feature_3:
Item intake with photos and value

Collect donated items through a form that asks for a photo, the fair market value and any expiry date. Each submission becomes a numbered catalog entry the committee can sort.
fields.feature_4:
Outbid emails during online auctions

Email a bidder the moment someone tops their bid, with the new high and a button to bid again. A week-long auction keeps people returning with no volunteer chasing them.
fields.feature_5:
Winner emails that state item value

List the price of each won item next to its stated value. The IRS allows a deduction only for the amount paid above that value, and the winner email shows both numbers.
fields.feature_6:
Your code on GitHub when you want it

Export the full codebase to your own GitHub repository once the auction grows into a year-round donor portal. Your developers host it on their own servers from then on.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Groups That Take Bids Online
fields.tab_content_1:
A $340 bid bounces when $350 is the floor

The Maple Grove Elementary spring gala puts 60 items on its tables, each with a QR code on its bid card. The Pine Lake cabin weekend sits at $325 with a $25 increment. A parent who enters $340 is asked to bid at least $350, and the bids table only ever holds valid bids.
fields.tab_content_2:
The donor's own value sets each opening bid

Donors fill in the value themselves when they give an item to the Cedar Hills Hospital Foundation gala, and each one uploads a photo. No opening bid is more than 40% of the stated value. A spa day valued at $500 opens at $200.
fields.tab_content_3:
Someone tops your bid and the email names the new high

Willow Creek Animal Rescue keeps its online auction open for 7 days. Jordan Lee had $165 on a handmade quilt until another bidder went to $180. Jordan got an email with the new high bid and a link to the quilt, where $190 retakes the lead.
fields.tab_content_4:
Bidding stops and each winner gets a pickup list

The Oak Valley Church fall festival closes its silent auction at 9:00 pm. The top bid on each of its 42 items becomes the winning bid. Every winner gets one email listing their items and the pickup table. Maria Ortiz won 3 items for $410 and collects them at table 4.

fields.howto_title: How to Build a Silent Auction Form
fields.howto_description: Settle the bidding rules and the closing time before you open the builder.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Choose paper, a form or both
fields.howto_step_1_des: Paper bid sheets suit a room of 40 guests and a dozen items. Once the item count climbs, or bidding runs online for days, a form does the tallying for you. Many galas keep a few printed sheets as a backup.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Give each donated item a number, a short description, a photo and the donor's name. Record the fair market value the donor states, plus any expiry date or restriction, such as dinner reservations valid on weeknights only.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Decide how opening bids and increments are set before the catalog goes out. Many organizers open at no more than half of fair market value. Round increments to a clean $10 or $25 so guests can do the math standing up.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Paste the item list and your bidding rules into one prompt. Emergent builds a bid page for every item and the bids table behind them, plus a view for the committee. Ask for a new increment or a later close and the form changes.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Print one QR code per item
fields.howto_step_5_des: Print each item's QR code on its table card, with the item number large enough to read from a step away. Online auctions skip the cards and send one catalog link by email and on your social pages instead.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Set the close and the winner email
fields.howto_step_6_des: Set the closing time to the minute and write the email winners receive. Name the pickup table and the hours volunteers staff it. Show each item's stated value next to the winning bid for the winner's records.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Run a test auction from two phones
fields.howto_step_7_des: Bid on one test item from two phones a day before the event. Try an amount under the increment, then let one phone top the other and check that the outbid email arrives. Close the test item and read the winner email.

plan.angle: The live top 10 is printable bid sheets: Etsy and Amazon packs, Pinterest boards, template posts from fundraising blogs, and an AI Overview that lists the fields a bid sheet needs and names Google Forms as the digital fallback. Every result stops at a sheet of paper that someone reads by hand at closing. This page shows the auction a form can run end to end: donated items logged with their value and opening bid, bids from a QR code at each table that must beat the high bid by the increment, outbid emails during a week-long online auction, and a winners list built the moment bidding closes.
